sections.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Ten Martini Cantor-spectrum conclusion on the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum for every nonconstant real-analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator, extending their method to intrinsic centers of arbitrary finite dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that for nonconstant real-analytic v and irrational frequency α, the spectrum intersected with the closure of the positive-Lyapunov-exponent energies is a Cantor set, when that intersection is nonempty (Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: One-frequency Schrödinger operators with real-analytic, nonconstant sampling function and irrational frequency; the conclusion is restricted to the closure of energies with positive Lyapunov exponent.
sections.unique_caveat: This paper guarantees that the whole spectrum is Cantor when the Lyapunov exponent is positive throughout it; it does not settle all zero-exponent energies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed extension removes the earlier Type-I restriction in the supercritical regime and links dynamical-systems and spectral-theory categories; an independent Wolfram MathWorld reference page also records the result.

sections.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
sections.abstract: Using an unconditional variant of Montgomery’s pair-correlation method, the author improves Selberg’s explicit bound: a positive proportion of consecutive nontrivial zeta zeros have normalized gap at most 0.7892.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves D(λ)>0 for every λ≥0.7892, which gives a positive proportion of consecutive zero ordinates with γₙ₊₁−γₙ≤2πλ/log γₙ (Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity; the result is unconditional and concerns a positive proportion, not all consecutive gaps.
sections.unique_caveat: The constant is not claimed optimal: the author notes that a more complicated explicit kernel already yields λ>0.7864, and further optimization may improve it.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It improves a long-standing explicit unconditional threshold from 1−2.36×10⁻⁶ to 0.7892, a concrete quantitative advance in analytic number theory; the paper states its result as Theorem 1.1.

sections.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
sections.abstract: The author proves that the numerical range of a finite complex matrix has constant width d exactly when it is a closed disk of radius d/2, with a singleton in the zero-width case.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the conjectured equivalence between constant width d and being a closed disk of radius d/2 (allowing a singleton when d=0), and derives the corresponding quadratic factor of the Kippenhahn polynomial (Theorem 1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Classical numerical range of a finite-dimensional complex matrix; the width is measured in every planar direction.
sections.unique_caveat: The argument concerns the classical numerical range only; it does not establish the analogous conjecture for higher-rank numerical ranges.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concise, complete resolution of a named matrix-analysis conjecture, with a structural consequence for the Kippenhahn polynomial stated in the abstract.

sections.title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
sections.abstract: For the split four-nodal Cayley cubic over Q with its nine lines removed, the author proves the rational-point asymptotic N_U(B)∼c_Peyre B(log B)^6 for the specified maximum-coordinate height.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves N_U(B)=c_Peyre B(log B)^6+o(B(log B)^6) as B→∞ and identifies the constant from the effective-cone volume and local densities (Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rational points on the split four-nodal Cayley cubic surface over Q after removing its nine lines, ordered by the paper’s bounded maximum-coordinate height.
sections.unique_caveat: The asymptotic is for this particular open surface and height; it does not by itself settle analogous counts on the removed boundary lines or other cubic surfaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a precise Peyre-constant asymptotic while combining universal-torsor parametrization, lattice counting and Poisson summation; this is a concrete arithmetic-geometric theorem, not merely a proposed bound.

sections.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
sections.abstract: The authors combine Artin–Tate formulas over finite extensions with lattice sphere-packing bounds to derive necessary conditions on K3 Weil polynomials, excluding about 52.53% of the listed candidates over F₂.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive special-value constraints at roots of unity from a refined Artin–Tate formula and lattice discriminant bounds; their computation excludes 878,580 of 1,672,565 candidate Weil polynomials over F₂ (about 52.53%).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: K3 surfaces over finite fields, with the explicit enumeration applied to candidate Weil polynomials over F₂; the inequalities are necessary conditions, not a classification.
sections.unique_caveat: The filtering leaves 793,985 candidates in the reported F₂ list, and surviving candidates are not thereby proved to arise from K3 surfaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It supplies a cross-field bridge from Frobenius lattices to sphere-packing bounds and reports a checkable finite-candidate reduction: 878,580 of 1,672,565 F₂ candidates are excluded by the combined conditions.

sections.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
sections.abstract: The author shows that a very general cubic threefold is determined up to isomorphism among smooth cubic threefolds by its stable birational equivalence class, and indicates extensions to other Fano threefolds.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that if a smooth cubic threefold is stably birational to a very general cubic threefold X, then it is isomorphic to X; the method also applies to the sextic double solid and quartic threefold (abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Very general smooth cubic threefolds over the paper’s algebraic-geometric setting, compared only with smooth cubic threefolds; examples of other Fano 3-folds are discussed.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s strongest uniqueness statement is for very general cubic threefolds; it does not assert the same classification for every special cubic or every higher-dimensional Fano variety.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states a sharp rigidity result for a central birational-equivalence relation and applies its method to other named Fano threefold families; the higher-dimensional case is also discussed.

sections.title: A counterexample to the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture in dimensions three and higher
sections.abstract: The author constructs compact sets satisfying the interior r-sphere condition that disprove the strong union-of-balls conjecture in every dimension n≥3 and show that the universal covering radius r/2 is sharp there.
sections.claimed_result: For every n≥3, r>0 and ε>0, the author constructs a compact S⊂Rⁿ satisfying the interior r-sphere condition with a point uncovered by every contained ball of radius (1/2+ε)r; hence r/2 cannot be improved (Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean Rⁿ, n≥3, compact sets with the interior r-sphere condition; the planar case has a different optimal radius.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction disproves the strong conjecture only in dimensions n≥3; the paper cites the planar theorem with the distinct sharp radius r/√3.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It resolves the conjecture’s dimensional boundary with explicit compact counterexamples and sharpens the geometric picture by separating the planar optimum r/√3 from the higher-dimensional r/2 threshold.

sections.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
sections.abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, the authors prove Lam’s determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix on bounded chambers and construct a Koszul duality yielding explicit multivariate formulas in the normal-crossing case.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Lam’s determinant conjecture for the bounded-chamber restriction of the inverse Varchenko matrix; for normal-crossing arrangements, a Koszul duality between two constructed algebras gives an explicit multivariate formula (abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Real affine hyperplane arrangements; the Koszul-duality construction is stated for normal-crossing arrangements, with possible generalization to affine oriented matroids discussed.
sections.unique_caveat: The explicit Koszul-duality statement is for normal-crossing arrangements; the extension to affine oriented matroids is discussed rather than established in the abstract as a full general theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work connects combinatorics, algebraic geometry and representation theory and proves both a named determinant conjecture and a further determinant conjecture of the authors, supported by an explicit algebraic construction.

sections.title: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
sections.abstract: The authors establish concavity of Rényi entropy and entropy power for orders α∈[1,2] along Euclidean heat flow and, under a curvature-dimension condition, along Witten-Laplacian heat flow on complete Riemannian manifolds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the stated concavity results under the paper’s hypotheses and establish complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order 2, including a spectral decomposition (abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean space in arbitrary dimension for Rényi orders α∈[1,2]; more generally complete Riemannian manifolds with Witten Laplacian under a suitable curvature-dimension condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The manifold extension depends on a curvature-dimension condition and analytic regularity/integrability hypotheses; this is not an unrestricted result for every heat flow or entropy order.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete extension from Euclidean inequalities to weighted Riemannian geometry, cross-listed in differential geometry, information theory and probability; the abstract also reports complete monotonicity at Tsallis order 2.

sections.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
sections.abstract: For focusing energy-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with damping a(1+t)⁻ᶿ, the authors establish global existence and scattering/non-scattering thresholds across mass-subcritical, mass-critical and intercritical regimes, with a conjectured sharp threshold at θ=1.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove scattering for the stated mass-subcritical and critical cases, a small-data result and scattering/grow-up dichotomy in the intercritical case; for θ=1 they reduce to an NLS with decaying repulsive harmonic potential and construct approximate solitary waves with integrable error (abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Focusing NLS with linear damping a(1+t)⁻ᶿ, a>0, in the whole energy-subcritical range; thresholds depend on θ and on mass/energy regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact sharpness of the θ=1 scattering threshold remains a conjecture supported by numerical simulations; the paper’s conclusions vary across the mass regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives regime-dependent global/scattering thresholds and an exact reduction at the scale-invariant damping rate θ=1, linking PDE analysis with an explicitly stated, numerically supported sharpness conjecture.

sections.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
sections.abstract: The author rules out a 13-vertex simplicial triangulation of the three-torus, narrowing its minimum possible vertex count to 14 or 15.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves there is no simplicial triangulation of T³ on 13 vertices, yielding 14≤v(T³)≤15 (Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simplicial triangulations of the three-torus; a known 15-vertex example gives the upper bound.
sections.unique_caveat: The 14-vertex case remains unresolved by this result, so vertex-minimality of the 15-vertex construction is not yet decided.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It closes one of two specific cases left open by standard lower-bound arguments and combines a g₂ inequality, simplicial-complement reduction, fundamental groups and Alexander duality; it is cross-listed in topology and combinatorics.
